enter_pairing_mode.indicator: On most HC-05 / HC-06 boards the status LED blinks quickly while unpaired and discoverable.
enter_pairing_mode.notes: A slave-mode module is discoverable and pairable whenever it is powered and not connected. There is no button: the only way to change the PIN or clear its pairing list is the module's AT command mode, which needs a wire to the module itself.

exclusivity.notes: A slave-mode HC-05 / HC-06 serves one SPP link at a time. Whether a given module keeps several remembered pairings is firmware-dependent and irrelevant to a passive check, so it is not stated.
exclusivity.recovery: Not something this app ever needs: it never connects. For anyone verifying with the Skimmer Scanner, a module that is already linked to another phone will not answer until that link drops.

pairing.notes: These are Bluetooth Classic serial (SPP) modules, Bluetooth 2.0-era parts that use legacy PIN pairing with no Secure Simple Pairing, so pairing happens in the host's Bluetooth settings with the PIN above before any serial channel opens. That is the step the SparkFun Skimmer Scanner automates: pair with 1234, open the serial channel, send 'P', and treat an 'M' reply as the skimmer firmware's tell. This spec deliberately does none of it — it matches the advertised name passively and never pairs — so this block describes the module class, not anything this integration does. Medium confidence rests on the SparkFun open-source app and the module family's published defaults; this project has not paired with one.

pin.notes: The HC-05 / HC-06 factory default, and the value the SparkFun Skimmer Scanner pairs with. Some HC-05 batches ship with 0000 instead. It is a product-wide constant, not a secret — and leaving it unchanged is part of the skimmer tell, because the criminal's phone needs to unlock the module without ever touching it again.

security_advisory.detail: Credit-card skimmers hidden in gas pumps, ATMs and card readers often use an off-the-shelf serial Bluetooth module (commonly an HC-05 or HC-06) left at its factory-default name and PIN, so the criminal's phone can find and unlock it. This device is advertising exactly that default name. That does NOT make it a skimmer — the same modules fill innocent hobby electronics, and the name alone cannot tell them apart. What separates the two is the skimmer firmware: the free SparkFun "Skimmer Scanner" app connects to an "HC-05" with the default PIN 1234, sends the letter 'P', and a real skimmer replies 'M'. This app scans passively over BLE and never connects, so it cannot run that check for you. If you see this AT a fuel pump, ATM or checkout, treat it with suspicion: don't pay there, verify with the Skimmer Scanner, and report it to the station or store operator (in the U.S., your state's weights-and-measures or agriculture department).

mitigation.summary: Confirm before you worry: the SparkFun "Skimmer Scanner" app connects to the module (default PIN 1234), sends 'P', and flags it only if it replies 'M' — the skimmer firmware's tell. A bare hobby module will not answer.

security_advisory.summary: A bare Bluetooth serial module left at its factory-default name. Harmless in hobby gear, but it is also what card skimmers use — worth a check if it is near a card reader.

credentials.notes: No credential crosses to this app; it never connects.

factory_reset.effect: Not applicable — this app never connects to or configures the device, so it has nothing to reset. Any real reset is done at the device.

methods.description: Passive: the device advertises over BLE, we match the exact default name and note it. No connection is made.

setup.notes: Nothing to set up: this app never connects to the device. It recognises the BLE advertisement and raises a soft heads-up; the match is inferred from the advertised name (see testing.notes), hence low confidence.

rejoin.notes: Recognised on sight wherever it advertises; nothing is stored.

testing.notes: Heuristic, not hardware-verified. Matches the HC-05 / HC-06 module name (we dropped HC-03 / HC-08 / FREE2MOVE). These are Bluetooth Classic modules, so whether one surfaces in a BLE scan is module-dependent, and the same modules fill innocent hobby projects — so this is a soft heads-up to verify, never proof.
